label: Calder Vale Rowing Trust — one programme in two house templates
covers: The same programme is set out twice in the same file using two DIFFERENT templates: a canonical five-column grid on slide 1, then the same content on slide 3 as headerless boxes with inline 'Label:' prefixes. This is distinct from two-versions-one-model, where both drafts use the same grid and only the wording differs; here the second pass also changes the SHAPE the reader has to recognise, which is the situation the owner described in the one real document that fails the launch gate on item count. The owner decided on 2026-09-28 that a reader should see each item once, so the FIRST pass is expected in the columns and the restating second pass is expected in unmapped: dropping it altogether still shows as lost recall, and mapping it into the columns a second time shows as misplacement. Two captures of this document on prompt 2026-09-26.1 from byte-identical input disagreed about which of those two things to do, which is why the rule is now written into the prompt and measured here.

columns.heading: RESOURCES
items: A coaching launch and eight stable training sculls
Two qualified coaches employed for the season

columns.heading: ACTIVITIES
items: An eight-week beginners course each spring and autumn
Free Saturday taster mornings open to the whole town

columns.heading: OUTPUTS
items: Ninety-six beginner places filled across the two courses
Twenty taster mornings run over the season

columns.heading: SHORT-TERM OUTCOMES
items: Beginners can scull a length unaided by the final week
Beginners say they feel safe on the water

columns.heading: LONG-TERM OUTCOMES
items: The club draws its membership from the whole town rather than one school
Rowing should not be something you need a particular school to reach. The pages that follow restate the model above in the format the trust uses with its funders.
Equipment: a launch for the coach and eight wide-beam boats for novices
Staffing: a pair of coaches contracted for the rowing season
Courses: two beginner intakes a year, each running eight weeks
Open days: taster sessions every Saturday with no booking needed
Places: ninety-six novices taught between the spring and autumn intakes
Sessions: twenty open mornings delivered through the season
Skill: novices complete a length on their own before the course ends
Confidence: novices report feeling secure in a boat
Reach: the membership stops depending on a single feeder school
